searchText: Am a single testnet validator runner for the past couple weeks (been doing it to practice before I switch to mainnet) Have shut down my all my clients, and will wait for more instructions on what the best next thing to do is. I assume updating will cause a slash event. I'm new to running a node, and finding it super interesting to see how teams are coordinating to revive holesky! Also starting to better understand where to follow things.. Are there public beacon endpoints available for holesky to exit validators? My clients are not syncing even after adding recommended enr's/enode's etc. I think to support the network it would be best if I exit my validators for now but I need a synced chain. exits aren’t possible until finality is restored, so although we appreciate the thought, exiting now would not help (vs exiting later) No need to exit, but shutting them down is helpful. Fewer attestations on wrong chains True , should have thought twice about this suggestion 🫤 . Ok, will do so! Are you sure? Isn't the idea to leave as many validators up as possible as long as they have their slashing protection enabled? From what I can glean the priority is getting as many validators _proposing_ as possible, i.e. attestation is a separate thing see here: https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/892088344438255616/1344276820517978172 and here: https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/892088344438255616/1344278056818311239 _if_ you have time and energy to sync to the correct chain: do it. If not: shutdown. good info here for lighthouse btw: https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/issues/7040 Is there a link to the 2pm call? https://ethereumfoundation.zoom.us/j/86466169680?pwd=x17cbD1lDCeQEWMTTOLARQhELiJV21.1 this is what's in the calendar event. Per <@602753420033785856>'s question in <#892088344438255616> about whether to add a flag to CL clients to temporarily censor slashings to help Holesky finalize, my (a solo staker's) take is that it's a pandora's box. If that flag is added to clients, and if this situation were ever to occur on mainnet, I think there would be a huge amount of pressure from everyone staking on the "wrong" side of the fork to a) activate this flag (so they don't get slashed rejoining the correct fork), and b) to either leave it active indefinitely, or to implement some kind of corollary "amnesty" logic to guarantee that they wouldn't be punished for their clients having bugs. There might actually be some value in thinking more about what such a socially-activated "amnesty" might look like, in the case of a supermajority bug like this, but IMO including a way to deactivate slashing on CLs should only be done if we have already thought through the mainnet game theory carefully. Once it's implemented in clients it will likely be hard to go back to how things were before, where slashing was just assumed to be unavoidable in cases like this. As good as it is to work out the technical side of a recovery like this, on mainnet there's going to be a huge amount of pressure to find some way to avoid slashing 2/3+ of the stake. As is, recovering holesky depends on the majority being willing to get back on the minority fork, and propose enough blocks so that their own slashings can be processed and get the chain back to finality. That won't happen willingly on mainnet.
